headline: JPMorgan is offering lenders a yield of about 11% on a $5 billion loan for the new AI cloud company Volta, one of the highest borrowing costs seen in this market.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: Bloomberg reports a new high in borrowing cost for AI chip and data-centre debt, but the terms come from one unnamed person and the deal is not closed.
importance_line: Investors who buy risky AI debt are being offered about 11% and AI computing firms face borrowing costs that high, but the loan has no credit rating, the terms come from one unnamed person and lenders have until 14 October to commit.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Yahoo Finance UK, that JPMorgan is marketing a $5 billion loan for Volta Infrastructure, a new AI cloud company, at terms that Bloomberg calculates as a yield of roughly 11%, a new high for this kind of AI loan. The money would buy about 36,000 Nvidia chips and secure the lease of a Norway data centre where Anthropic has signed a six-year deal for computing power, though the loan has no credit rating and lenders have until 14 October to commit, according to people familiar.
